item.text:
I treated your local prior as the structured baseline and did not re-fetch the country-year datasets already supplied there. The additions below are only for ruler attribution, office/authority/constraint framing, and 2022 narrative context.

**Bottom Line**
- Jokowi in 2022 was Indonesia’s president in his second and final constitutional term, having been inaugurated on October 20, 2019.
- Formally, he held executive power, could propose bills, issue implementing regulations, appoint and dismiss ministers, and command the armed forces, but he operated inside hard limits: a five-year term with only one reelection, legislative bargaining, judicial review, fiscal constraints, and public backlash.
- For 2022, the main cross-chapter narrative is: post-pandemic recovery under inflation/subsidy pressure, the new-capital push, a cabinet reshuffle, the fuel-price shock and protests, the Kanjuruhan disaster and accountability response, and the G20 summit in Bali.
- The local facts you supplied already cover the structured country-year evidence for Chapters 2B-8B, so this source set is for narrative attribution and event framing, not scoring.

**Retained Source Families**
- Primary / official: Presidency Secretariat, Cabinet Secretariat, BPK JDIH, MKRI, BPS.
- Independent / local-language: Kompas.
- State / favorable: ANTARA.
- Independent wire: Reuters syndicated through Euronews.

**Office, Authority, Constraints**
- [Presiden Joko Widodo dan Wakil Presiden Ma’ruf Amin Dilantik di MPR](https://presidenri.go.id/siaran-pers/presiden-joko-widodo-dan-wakil-presiden-maruf-amin-dilantik-di-mpr/) - **Presiden RI**, October 20, 2019. Precise fact: Jokowi and Ma’ruf Amin were inaugurated for the 2019-2024 term. Period fit: establishes his office in 2022. Ruler attribution: direct, because it is the presidency officeholder record. Limitations: inauguration does not by itself show policy performance. Contrary points: none on the office fact itself.
- [Indonesia 1945 (rev. 2002) Constitution](https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Indonesia_2002) - **Constitute Project** (official constitutional text translation), current consolidated text. Precise fact: the president holds executive power, may submit bills, may issue regulations, is assisted by a vice president, and serves a five-year term with only one additional term possible. Period fit: defines Jokowi’s authority and term ceiling in 2022. Ruler attribution: institutional, not personal; it frames what Jokowi could do. Limitations: it is constitutional text, not practice. Contrary points: actual leverage can be narrower because of parties, courts, and budget politics.
- [UU No. 39 Tahun 2008 - Kementerian Negara](https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/39719/uu-no-39-tahun-2008) - **BPK JDIH**, November 6, 2008. Precise fact: ministries are under and responsible to the president; ministers manage specific government sectors. Period fit: explains cabinet control and the reshuffle logic in 2022. Ruler attribution: direct for ministerial appointments, indirect for policy outcomes. Limitations: does not tell us whether cabinet choices were effective. Contrary points: coalition bargaining and technocratic constraints may blunt presidential control.
- [Partai Berkarya Uji Masa Jabatan Presiden dan Wakil Presiden](https://www.mkri.id/berita/-18782) - **Mahkamah Konstitusi RI**, December 15, 2021. Precise fact: MK’s public explanation reiterates the two-term ceiling under Article 7. Period fit: confirms that 2022 was Jokowi’s final allowed term. Ruler attribution: directly relevant because it defines the legal ceiling on his tenure. Limitations: this is a case explanation, not a 2022 event record. Contrary points: none on the ceiling itself unless the constitution is amended.
- [President Jokowi Reshuffles Indonesia Onward Cabinet](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-reshuffles-indonesia-onward-cabinet/) - **Sekretariat Kabinet RI**, June 15, 2022. Precise fact: Jokowi installed new ministers and vice ministers for the remainder of the 2019-2024 period. Period fit: shows continuing executive agenda management inside 2022. Ruler attribution: direct. Limitations: reshuffles are input signals, not proof of policy success. Contrary points: the need to reshuffle can also indicate personnel or coalition instability.

**Major 2022 Events / Inherited Conditions**
- [Ratified Law on Capital Marks New Capital Development](https://setkab.go.id/en/ratified-law-on-capital-marks-new-capital-development/) - **Sekretariat Kabinet RI**, February 21, 2022. Precise fact: Law No. 3/2022 on the new capital was signed, giving the IKN project its legal basis. Period fit: a major 2022 agenda item. Ruler attribution: direct, because it is his administration’s legal-authority move. Limitations: legal basis is not the same as delivery. Contrary points: critics focused on cost, land, and prioritization.
- [President Jokowi Issues Directives on New Capital](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-issues-directives-on-new-capital/) - **Sekretariat Kabinet RI**, March 10, 2022. Precise fact: Jokowi ordered land and institutional preparation for IKN, including land-status verification. Period fit: shows implementation pressure in 2022. Ruler attribution: direct. Limitations: executive direction does not settle implementation risk. Contrary points: land and regulatory issues remained contested.
- [Indonesia hikes fuel prices to rein in ballooning subsidies](https://www.euronews.com/2022/09/04/indonesia-subsidies) - **Euronews citing Reuters**, September 4, 2022. Precise fact: subsidized fuel prices were raised by about 30% to contain subsidy spending; the move risked protests and inflation pressure. Period fit: key 2022 macro-political shock. Ruler attribution: direct, because the pricing decision was made by Jokowi’s government. Limitations: wire reporting compresses domestic policy detail. Contrary points: supporters would frame it as fiscal discipline and targeted aid.
- [Tiga Bantuan Sosial di Tengah Kenaikan Harga BBM](https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2022/09/03/17341821/tiga-bantuan-sosial-di-tengah-kenaikan-harga-bbm) - **Kompas.com**, September 3, 2022. Precise fact: the fuel-price hike triggered compensating cash-aid measures. Period fit: helps connect the subsidy shock to domestic politics and welfare tradeoffs. Ruler attribution: direct for the policy package, but not for all resulting hardship. Limitations: advocacy framing around relief measures. Contrary points: aid may not fully offset inflation or protest costs.
- [Selesai Dianalisis, Hasil Investigasi Tragedi Kanjuruhan Diserahkan ke Jokowi Jumat Siang](https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2022/10/13/21244011/selesai-dianalisis-hasil-investigasi-tragedi-kanjuruhan-diserahkan-ke-jokowi) - **Kompas.com**, October 13, 2022. Precise fact: the Kanjuruhan fact-finding process was being handed to Jokowi; the underlying tragedy followed the October 1, 2022 stadium disaster. Period fit: major internal-security / accountability event in 2022. Ruler attribution: Jokowi is the recipient of the report and the top political authority over the response, but not the sole operational actor. Limitations: this source is closer to reporting than final adjudication. Contrary points: police and sports-bureaucracy responsibility remained contested.
- [Jokowi officially opens 2022 G20 Summit in Bali](https://en.antaranews.com/news/260285/jokowi-officially-opens-2022-g20-summit-in-bali) - **ANTARA News**, November 15, 2022. Precise fact: Jokowi opened the G20 summit in Bali as Indonesia’s host. Period fit: major external-facing state-capacity event in 2022. Ruler attribution: direct. Limitations: host-success narratives emphasize ceremony and diplomacy. Contrary points: domestic critics could argue foreign-policy prestige did not resolve internal governance problems.
- [Indonesia announces adoption of Bali Leaders' Declaration](https://en.antaranews.com/news/260617/g20-summit-indonesia-announces-adoption-of-bali-leaders-declaration) - **ANTARA News**, November 16, 2022. Precise fact: Indonesia announced adoption of the Bali Leaders’ Declaration and handed the G20 presidency to India. Period fit: closes the year’s flagship diplomatic event. Ruler attribution: direct. Limitations: official coverage highlights success and downplays negotiation costs. Contrary points: declaration language can be a diplomatic minimum, not a policy breakthrough.
- [The inflation in September 2022 was 1.17 percent](https://www.bps.go.id/id/pressrelease/2022/10/03/1865/inflasi-terjadi-pada-september-2022-inflasi-sebesar-1-17-persen--inflasi-tertinggi-terjadi-di-bukittinggi-sebesar-1-87-persen-.htm/) - **BPS Statistics Indonesia**, October 3, 2022. Precise fact: September 2022 inflation was 1.17 percent. Period fit: directly captures the cost-of-living backdrop to the fuel-price decision. Ruler attribution: contextual, not personal. Limitations: monthly inflation does not itself explain policy causation. Contrary points: inflation can be driven by global prices, not only domestic governance.
- [Indonesia GDP Growth Rate 5.31 Percent (2022)](https://www.bps.go.id/en/pressrelease/2023/02/06/1997/ekonomi-indonesia-tahun-2022-tumbuh-5-31-persen) - **BPS Statistics Indonesia**, February 6, 2023. Precise fact: Indonesia’s 2022 economy grew 5.31 percent and GDP per capita reached about US$4,783.9. Period fit: year-end inherited condition for 2022 performance. Ruler attribution: contextual, not a personal-success proof. Limitations: aggregate growth hides distribution and governance gaps. Contrary points: growth did not eliminate civil-liberty, corruption, or accountability concerns.

**Compact Event Map**
- February 15-21, 2022: IKN law signed and publicly framed as the legal start of the new capital project.
- March 10, 2022: Jokowi issued operational directives on IKN land and institutional preparation.
- June 15, 2022: cabinet reshuffle signaled active executive control over the administration.
- September 3-6, 2022: fuel-price hike and protest cycle exposed fiscal strain and popular resistance.
- October 1-13, 2022: Kanjuruhan became a major accountability and public-order crisis.
- November 15-16, 2022: G20 in Bali gave Jokowi a high-visibility foreign-policy stage and a claim to state-capacity success.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- 1B: keep the local prior only for now; it already says no evidence was found. If later needed, use FAS and NTI, but only if a 1B narrative is actually required.
- 2B: local UCDP/SIPRI prior plus the fuel-price shock and protest context if narrative detail is needed.
- 3B: local CIRIGHTS/PTS/V-Dem/UCDP prior plus Kompas on Kanjuruhan for ruler-attributed security and repression context.
- 4B: Constitution, inauguration, term-limit ruling, ministry law, reshuffle, and Kanjuruhan/fuel-protest context for freedom, opposition pressure, and executive constraints.
- 5B: BPS GDP growth, inflation, and IKN/fuel-policy context for economic scale and inherited conditions.
- 6B: local health/HDI prior is already enough; no new source family is necessary unless you want ruler-specific welfare attribution.
- 7B: ministry law, MK/constitutional framework, and Kanjuruhan/fuel-policy accountability context for corruption and institutional control.
- 8B: Constitution, ministry law, IKN directives, reshuffle, and G20 delivery for governance-capacity and executive coordination.
- Cross-chapter rule: use the local prior first, and only pull in external sources when you need ruler attribution, narrative detail, or a source family not already represented in the structured facts.
